terms.comment: A ball of the lands. Cicero calls the earth itself a globe: illum globum … quae terra dīcitur (Rep. 6.15), and gives globus as the Latin for σφαῖρα (N. D. 2.47).

terms.gloss: a sphere; a model globe, classically of the heavens
terms.comment: Archimedes’ sphere, which showed the courses of the sun, the moon and the planets, was a sphaera (Cic. Rep. 1.21–22).

phrases.latin: Hominēs enim sunt hāc lēge generātī, quī tuērentur illum globum, quem in hōc templō medium vidēs, quae terra dīcitur
phrases.english: For men were born on these terms, to look after that globe you see in the middle of this temple, which is called the earth

phrases.latin: Quaere in globō ubi sit Lūsitānia.
